newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - Scanty buying to push SE Asian prices lower.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - Scanty buying to push SE Asian prices lower.

text.p: Southeast Asian rubber prices will probably slide further this week as thin buying interest weighs on the market, regional traders said on Monday.
"My money is on prices going down," the head of one rubber division in a Singapore-based trade house told Reuters. "Demand is quiet all around. The basic trend is still bearish."
"I think the market will weaken further this week," a rubber dealer in Jakarta said. "Buyers have either shown little interest or have been bidding well below offers."
Most of the major consumers from the U.S. and Europe have already put on coverage for December and will be taking a look at their January/February requirements, dealers said.
"But they are not in a hurry to get that coverage because they believe prices will still come off. It's quite a gloomy market," a Singapore-based trader said.
"I think interest will come mostly from Japanese buyers either directly or through Singapore agents next week," an Indonesian dealer added. "I see prices going down by 0.25 (U.S.) cents/lb."

Poor demand all week saw tyre-grade SIR20 offer prices in Indonesia ease 0.25 U.S. cents to 56.00-56.25 cents/lb FOB Medan, 55.50-55.75 cents FOB Palembang, Padang and Surabaya, 55.125 cents FOB Jambi and 55.00 cents FOB Pontianak.
Latex was generally stable at 2,300-2,400 rupiah/kg.
Malaysian traders said they expected the market to trade in a tight range this week.
Buyers were expecting lower prices while producers were holding to current levels on expectations of a tightness in the supply of raw materials, the traders added.
Consumer demand is still weak in the local market and is not expected to improve much in the near term, they said.

The December buying price for benchmark RSS1 rubber was seen at 317.50 Malaysian cents a kg at the close of the market last week while SMR20 was at 310.50 cents. Latex was quoted by trading houses at 239 cents a kg on Friday.
"I expect both the RSS1 and SMR20 to rise two to three cents this week," a trader said.
One dealer said steady rain in Malaysia's northern rubber farms had led to tightness in the supply of raw materials, especially latex, and producers were reluctant to cut prices.
The Malaysian Meteorological Services Department said it expected more rains in peninsular Malaysia this week.
In Thailand, the market was mostly steady last week with exporters generally cautious ahead of last Saturday's general election, dealers said.
"Some are reluctant to commit for fears that the local prices might rise," one Bangkok-based trader said.
"But demand seemed to pick up as buyers sought to cover demand for the first quarter of 1997," said another trader from Hat Yai.
There have been some buying orders and inquiries from China, Japan and Europe, trade sources said.
Traders said they see export prices moving in the current range until the end of the year as higher demand will be offset by more supply after the monsoon season ends.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for December shipment was quoted around US$1.24-$1.26 a kg FOB Bangkok at the end of last week, barely changed from a week previously.
STR20 for the same shipment was quoted around $1.23-$1.24 a kg on Friday from $1.24 the previous week. Latex edged down slightly to 94 U.S. cents a kg on thin demand.
(With contributions from Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia)
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
